segments.source: Density compares an amount with the space available. It can reveal crowding even when two places have similar total populations.
Given facts.
A park zone covers 7 hectares and currently has 42 visitors. For this exercise, comfortable density is at most 7 visitors per hectare.
Rules.
Density = number ÷ area. A zone exceeds comfortable capacity if density is greater than the stated threshold.
Task.
What is the visitor density, and is the zone above the stated comfortable capacity?
Step-by-step solution.
1. Density=42÷7=6.00 visitors/hectare. 2. Compare 6.00 with the threshold 7.
Answer.
6.00 visitors/hectare; within capacity.
Knowledge takeaway.
Totals and densities answer different questions; always identify the denominator.
Formal model.
Ratio density=N/A followed by threshold comparison.

N6. Land use and spatial compatibility
Problem 401. Land-use compatibility on four plots: case 1
Knowledge context.
Land-use planning combines spatial relationships with compatibility rules.
Given facts.

Four plots lie in a line A–B–C–D. Assign one different use to each plot: school, factory, park, homes. Constraints: the factory may not be adjacent to the school; the park must be adjacent to the homes. Cross-domain check: a survey team starts work at 8:00 and works for 2 hour(s) without a break.
Rules.
An assignment is valid only if every use is placed exactly once and all adjacency constraints hold. For the cross-domain check, finishing time = starting time + duration.
Task.
Give one valid assignment and explain why it satisfies every constraint. Cross-domain check: at what time does the team finish?
Step-by-step solution.

1. Try the assignment A=school, B=park, C=homes, D=factory. 2. Factory and school are not adjacent. 3. Park and homes are adjacent. 4. Each use appears exactly once. Cross-domain check: 8+2=10, so the team finishes at 10:00.
Answer.
A=school, B=park, C=homes, D=factory is a valid assignment. Cross-domain answer: 10:00.
Knowledge takeaway.
A place can be unsuitable not because of its own properties, but because of what would be next to it.
Formal model.
Permutation CSP with all-different and adjacency/non-adjacency constraints.
Problem 402. Land-use compatibility on four plots: case 2
Knowledge context.
Land-use planning combines spatial relationships with compatibility rules.
Given facts.

Four plots lie in a line A–B–C–D. Assign one different use to each plot: school, factory, park, homes. Constraints: the factory may not be adjacent to the school; the park must be adjacent to the homes. Cross-domain check: a local committee has 14 members, requires at least 8 present for quorum, and 14 are present.
Rules.
An assignment is valid only if every use is placed exactly once and all adjacency constraints hold. For the cross-domain check, quorum exists when present members ≥ the stated threshold.
Task.
Give one valid assignment and explain why it satisfies every constraint. Cross-domain check: is quorum met?
Step-by-step solution.

1. Try the assignment A=school, B=homes, C=park, D=factory. 2. Factory and school are not adjacent. 3. Park and homes are adjacent. 4. Each use appears exactly once. Cross-domain check: compare 14 with 8; 14≥8 is true.
Answer.
A=school, B=homes, C=park, D=factory is a valid assignment. Cross-domain answer: quorum is met.
Knowledge takeaway.
A place can be unsuitable not because of its own properties, but because of what would be next to it.
Formal model.
Permutation CSP with all-different and adjacency/non-adjacency constraints.
